findings.summary: NoCallerFilePathAnalyzer.AnalyzeAttribute duplicates the whole match-then-report function body already written for AG0008's AnalyzeAttribute — not just the shared sub-helpers, the entire method.
findings.evidence: analyzers/AgentGuard.Analyzers/NoCallerFilePathAnalyzer.cs:76-90 vs analyzers/AgentGuard.Analyzers/InteropOnlyInCrossPlatformLibrariesAnalyzer.cs:69-84. Both methods: cast context.Node to AttributeSyntax, call AttributeIdentity.IsAnyOf(context.SemanticModel, attribute, <identity-set>, context.CancellationToken) and early-return on false, then compute `string qualifiedName = AttributeSyntaxName.FullName(AttributeSyntaxName.SimpleName(attribute.Name));` and call `context.ReportDiagnostic(Diagnostic.Create(Rule, attribute.GetLocation(), qualifiedName));`. Confirmed the two-line reporting tail is byte-identical via grep -n 'AttributeSyntaxName.FullName(AttributeSyntaxName.SimpleName' across analyzers/AgentGuard.Analyzers/*.cs, which returns exactly these two analyzer files (plus AttributeIdentity.cs's own internal use for the syntactic-fallback tier, which is the legitimate single owner of that line — the two ANALYZER copies are the violation). This is rail #6 (duplicated block/whole function): the rule-gen agent reused the lower-level helpers (AttributeIdentity, AttributeSyntaxName) correctly, but re-wrote the enclosing 'match an attribute identity set and report its qualified name' function instead of calling a shared owner, growing a pattern the codebase's own AttributeIdentity.cs doc already calls out as a 'LESSON 1, DRY' extraction target one layer down. NativeCallbackBodyMustBeGuardedAnalyzer.cs (AG0104/AG0105) also calls AttributeIdentity.IsAnyOf but reports on a different node (an identifier, not the attribute's own qualified name, at line 271) so it is not a third copy of this exact shape — this is a 2-copy violation, both attribute-ban rules that report the attribute's own qualified name.
findings.fix: Extract the shared body into one owner, e.g. `internal static void ReportIfMatch(SyntaxNodeAnalysisContext context, DiagnosticDescriptor rule, ImmutableArray<(string Namespace, string Name)> candidates)` living beside AttributeIdentity (it already owns IsAnyOf and the two sub-helpers this composes). Give it the cast, the IsAnyOf check, the qualifiedName computation, and the ReportDiagnostic call. Rewrite InteropOnlyInCrossPlatformLibrariesAnalyzer.AnalyzeAttribute to `AttributeIdentity.ReportIfMatch(context, Rule, PInvoke.InteropAttributes);` (its CompilationStart cross-platform-library gate around RegisterSyntaxNodeAction is untouched — that policy stays at the AG0008 call site) and NoCallerFilePathAnalyzer.AnalyzeAttribute to `AttributeIdentity.ReportIfMatch(context, Rule, CallerFilePathAttribute);`. This touches InteropOnlyInCrossPlatformLibrariesAnalyzer.cs, a file outside this contract's declared rule-phase surface, so the collapse needs a scope note/sign-off before landing — flag that, don't silently expand scope.
